q: On March 1, Brightwater Supply purchased $9,000 of inventory on account, terms 2/10, n/30. On March 8 it paid the full amount due. Using the gross method, the journal entry to record the March 8 payment includes:
opts: Debit Accounts Payable $9,000; credit Purchase Discounts $180; credit Cash $8,820
Debit Cash $8,820; debit Purchase Discounts $180; credit Accounts Payable $9,000
rationale: Paying within the 10-day window earns a 2% discount (0.02 x $9,000 = $180), so the $9,000 payable is removed, $8,820 cash paid, and $180 credited to Purchase Discounts. Option B wrongly reduces the recorded payable; C ignores the discount taken; D reverses the debit/credit direction.

q: Cedar Lane Co. began the year with $42,000 of accounts receivable and ended with $51,000. During the year it reported $310,000 of credit sales and wrote off $4,000 of uncollectible accounts. How much cash did Cedar Lane collect from customers during the year?
rationale: Beginning AR + credit sales - write-offs - collections = ending AR. So 42,000 + 310,000 - 4,000 - collections = 51,000, giving collections = $297,000. The other options omit the write-off, ignore the balance change, or add instead of subtract.

q: Harbor Freight Inc. uses periodic FIFO. It had beginning inventory of 100 units at $8, purchased 200 units at $10, then 150 units at $12. It sold 300 units during the period. What is cost of goods sold?
rationale: FIFO expenses the oldest units first: 100 x $8 = $800, then 200 x $10 = $2,000, totaling 300 units for COGS of $2,800. $3,400 would be LIFO; the others mix layers incorrectly.

q: Summit Tools bought a machine for $60,000 with a $5,000 salvage value and a 5-year useful life, using double-declining-balance depreciation. What is depreciation expense in Year 2?
rationale: DDB rate = 2/5 = 40%, ignoring salvage in the rate. Year 1 = 40% x $60,000 = $24,000, leaving book value $36,000. Year 2 = 40% x $36,000 = $14,400. $24,000 is Year 1; the $13,200/$22,000 options wrongly subtract salvage before applying the rate.

q: At year-end, Maple Accounting Services has performed $6,500 of consulting work for a client but has not yet billed or recorded it. The correct adjusting entry is:
opts: Debit Accounts Receivable $6,500; credit Service Revenue $6,500
Debit Service Revenue $6,500; credit Accounts Receivable $6,500
Debit Unearned Revenue $6,500; credit Service Revenue $6,500
rationale: This is an accrued revenue: revenue earned but not yet billed, so you debit a receivable and credit revenue. No cash has arrived (ruling out B), the direction is not reversed (C), and nothing was prepaid by the client (ruling out the unearned-revenue entry D).

q: Northstar Kayaks sells a kayak for $480. Variable cost per kayak is $300, and monthly fixed costs are $54,000. The company wants a monthly target profit of $18,000. How many kayaks must it sell to hit that target?
rationale: Contribution margin = $480 - $300 = $180. Units for target profit = (Fixed + Target) / CM = (54,000 + 18,000) / 180 = 400 kayaks. 300 is the break-even volume (54,000/180); the others misuse the formula.

q: Ironclad Bottling sets a standard of 2 lbs of resin per crate at $3.00/lb. In June it produced 5,000 crates and used 11,000 lbs of resin purchased at $2.80/lb. What are the direct materials price and quantity variances?
rationale: Price variance = (AP - SP) x AQ = (2.80 - 3.00) x 11,000 = -$2,200, i.e. $2,200 Favorable (paid less). Standard qty allowed = 5,000 x 2 = 10,000 lbs; Quantity variance = (AQ - SQ) x SP = (11,000 - 10,000) x 3.00 = $3,000 Unfavorable (used more). The others flip favorable/unfavorable or swap the two variances.

q: Velar Devices reports the following for last month: sales $900,000; variable costs $540,000; fixed costs $270,000. If sales rise 20% next month with no change in selling price, unit variable cost, or fixed costs, what will operating income be?
rationale: Current CM = 900,000 - 540,000 = $360,000 (40% ratio); current operating income = 360,000 - 270,000 = $90,000. A 20% sales rise lifts CM to $360,000 x 1.20 = $432,000; fixed costs stay flat, so income = 432,000 - 270,000 = $162,000. $90,000 is the current figure; $108,000 wrongly scales income by 20%; $126,000 scales CM by only the income's growth.
